title: Africa, New Orleans and American music
summary: He says American jazz and Ellington came from Africa.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: I went to hear Buddy Rich recording last year, record an album, this rock music. He brought drummon (inaudible) play here. He play two. (Inaudible) it's two

And (inaudible) good rhythms, but it's different. The drummer, they play like a bongo player and compare. That's how you hear, ah-puck, boom, buhprrt, puh-tuhrrt-bee-bee, tuh, buck-boom. That's what they play.

Where that concept comes from? And they go back. Now, we're going back now to where we can (inaudible). That's what the people today, they're curious, they want to talk about, they want to read about, they want to find about, because they tell you the truth. That's where they come from, New Orleans, and it start in Africa.

So that's what I say, Duke Ellington's band -- I baptize when I came here, I say, this is Afro-American. People say, what you mean? Huh? He ain't got nothing to do with the Africans. I say, that's what you think. You don't know your history. You're born here but your people, they create you (inaudible) over there.
They're the ones brought all that here, but -- there were nothing but Indian here, and Indian music ain't got nothing to do with American music.
So where'd you get the music? And the
European just want to waltz and all that.
